$comment: Herbicide and insecticide line items extracted by hand from ISU Ag Decision Maker A1-20 (FM 1712), 'Estimated Costs of Crop Production in Iowa - 2026', revised January 2026. The PDF is archived alongside this file because extension.iastate.edu serves an Anubis proof-of-work challenge to scripted clients and cannot be re-fetched automatically. Page numbers refer to the archived PDF.

source.title: Estimated Costs of Crop Production in Iowa - 2026
source.publication: Iowa State University Extension, Ag Decision Maker File A1-20 (FM 1712)
source.access_note: Manual download only. Scripted access is blocked.

nature: prescriptive budget - the cost of a recommended program at surveyed input prices, NOT a survey of realised grower spending. See assumptions.md section 6 for why this matters.

budgets.tillage: conventional (chisel plow, tandem disk, field cultivate)

budgets.note: No insecticide line: rotation breaks corn rootworm pressure. Continuous corn on page 2 carries $25.
Footnote 2: estimates exclude any insecticide or fungicide cost.

findings.tillage_gradient: Reduced tillage raises herbicide cost sharply - corn $56 conventional vs $83 strip/low-till (+48%), soybeans $75 vs $89 (+19%). Tillage substitutes for chemical weed control. Directly relevant to See & Spray: reduced-till operations carry both a larger herbicide bill and heavier reliance on residuals.
findings.vs_ers: ISU conventional corn herbicide alone ($56.00) exceeds the entire ERS Heartland 2025 `Chemicals` line ($49.23) and is 134% of the ERS-derived herbicide figure ($41.85). For soybeans the gap is larger: $75-89 vs $44.19 derived, i.e. 170-201%.
findings.unresolved: This gap decides the project's headline. See assumptions.md section 6 - ISU is prescriptive, ERS is realised survey spending, and both are legitimate. Neither is a defect in the other.

not_in_this_document: A1-20 gives a single herbicide total per budget. It does NOT split residual from non-residual, which is what the See & Spray addressable share needs. ISU WC 94 (herbicide guide, per-treatment pricing) is still the document that would convert that estimate into a measurement.
